sources.stockdonFactor: Run-up exceeded by 2% of waves on natural sandy beaches, R2% = 1.1 (0.35 βf √(H0 L0) + ½ √(H0 L0 (0.563 βf² + 0.004))) (Stockdon, Holman, Howd & Sallenger 2006, Coastal Engineering 53(7), 10 field experiments)
sources.dissipativeIribarren: Where ξ0 = βf / √(H0 / L0) is under 0.3 the run-up no longer depends on the slope: R2% = 0.043 √(H0 L0) (Stockdon et al. 2006)
sources.sandyMaxSlope: Stockdon's beaches reach a foreshore slope of about 1:7; a steeper or harder slope takes EurOtop's run-up
sources.eurotopFactor: Ru2% / Hm0 = 1.65 γf ξm-1,0, at most γf (4.0 − 1.5 / √ξm-1,0) (EurOtop 2018, eq. 5.1 and 5.2)
sources.wallSlope: EurOtop's run-up is measured on slopes; a shore steeper than 1:1 is taken as a wall, where the wave reflects into a standing wave twice its height whose crest stands one wave height over still water (linear clapotis)
sources.spectralPeriodRatio: EurOtop's spectral period Tm-1,0 is the peak period over 1.1 (EurOtop 2018, 4.2)
sources.slopeSearchBlocks: How far inland the foreshore's slope is read along the waves' path, steps taken as a ramp through their corners

sources.uprushFriction: The swash front's quadratic bed friction on a sandy beach, fitted to over 4,500 uprushes: about 0.007 (Puleo & Holland 2001, Coastal Engineering 43(1))
sources.lensDepthRatio: The bore collapsed at the shoreline throws a lens of water up the beach, h = (x_s − x)² / (9 g t²) (Shen & Meyer 1963), whose mean depth over its length is U² / 27 g

bedSources.conductivity: Hydraulic conductivity, m/s (Freeze & Cherry 1979, Groundwater, table 2.2): fine sand 1e-5 to 1e-4, gravel 1e-2 to 1e-1, silt and loam 1e-9 to 1e-5, unfractured rock nil
bedSources.roughness: EurOtop 2018 table 5.2: a smooth impermeable slope 1.0, two layers of rock on an impermeable core 0.55
bedSources.sandy: Whether Stockdon's beach run-up applies to a slope of this material up to sandyMaxSlope; others take EurOtop's

sources.reflectionFactor: Kr = tanh(a ξ^b), a = 0.167 (1 − exp(−3.2 γf)), b = 1.49 (γf − 0.38)² + 0.86 (Zanuttigh & van der Meer 2008, Coastal Engineering 55(10)), for every slope from a beach to a wall
sources.toeDepthWaveHeights: EurOtop 2018 5.3.4 reads a structure's average slope from 1.5 Hm0 below still water
sources.smoothingWavelengths: A wave sees a face only at the scale of its own length: the face's normal is averaged over a quarter wavelength, so a stair of blocks reflects as the straight wall it makes up
sources.smoothingMaxBlocks: Performance budget: the most blocks a normal is averaged over
sources.reachBlocks: How far from a face its reflection is drawn: the seabed read reaches this far around the player wherever it stands
sources.nonImpulsiveFactor: Water passing height Rc on a wall under waves that do not strike impulsively: q / √(g Hm0³) = 0.05 exp(−2.78 Rc / Hm0) (EurOtop 2018 eq. 7.5)
sources.impulsiveFactor: Under impulsive waves: q / √(g Hm0³) = 0.011 (Hm0 / (h s))^0.5 exp(−2.2 Rc / Hm0) for Rc / Hm0 below 1.35 (EurOtop 2018 eq. 7.7)
sources.impulsivePowerFactor: And above 1.35: 0.0014 (Hm0 / (h s))^0.5 (Rc / Hm0)^−3 (EurOtop 2018 eq. 7.8), continuous with eq. 7.7 at 1.35
sources.impulsiveToe: Waves strike impulsively where h² / (Hm0 Lm-1,0) ≤ 0.23 at the toe (Van der Meer & Bruce 2014, as EurOtop 2018 takes it)
sources.jetSpeedRatio: The highest vertical water speed measured at a wall under a breaking wave, 2.14 C, C the wave's celerity (Bullock et al. 2007, Coastal Engineering 54(8), large-scale tests)
sources.foamDecaySeconds: Whitecap foam's area-weighted decay time, 1.4 to 4.8 s between observation periods (Callaghan, Deane & Stokes 2012, JGR Oceans); the middle of that range
sources.smallestParcelSide: One particle stands for a cube of water this wide: vanilla's water splash particle is 0.15 across
sources.largestParcelSide: Performance budget: a strike too big for parcelsPerMetre draws fewer, larger parcels, up to the size of a block, keeping its volume
sources.parcelsPerMetre: Performance budget: the most particles one strike spends on a metre of face
sources.radiusBlocks: Performance budget: how far from the player strikes throw spray
sources.tickMilliseconds: How often the faces around the player are watched for a strike
sources.sprayScatterMetresPerSecond: How far spray spreads off the face: vanilla's water splash particles scatter by this much

sources.haloBlocks: How far beyond a chunk the band's water is looked for: more than the farthest a sheet runs in the heaviest sea the knee (waves.kneeMetres) lets through
sources.highestRiseBlocks: The highest ground a sheet is followed onto: the sea's ceiling height (waves.ceilingMetres), which no run-up passes
sources.refreshMinutes: How often, in game minutes, a loaded shore reads its sea again to grow or drain the band
